title: Threaded Request Sifter — Interactive Span Breadcrumbs & Journey Map
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Support engineers and SREs regularly need to go from a high-level request card to the exact span sequence and correlated requests that caused a production regression. Current Console trace surfaces are strong on waterfall timelines but lack an interactive breadcrumb/‘sifter’ that lets users peel layers of a request journey, compare sibling spans, and pivot quickly to correlated requests by correlation ID or tag.

Goal: Design an interactive 'Threaded Request Sifter' experience that lives inside request detail, combining: 1) a condensed span breadcrumb (compact visual tokens representing service->operation->span duration), 2) a horizontally-scrollable journey map that aligns spans to timeline and highlights branching/parallel execution, and 3) an affordance to pivot to correlated requests or open a quick-scan panel for cost/rollout metadata (model variant, deployment region, routing policy). The surface must be keyboard-accessible and perform well with traces up to ~500 spans.

Why it matters: This will reduce mean time to remediation by letting engineers find the causal span faster, reduce context switching between tracing and cost/rollout consoles, and provide PMs a faster path to validate rollout-related regressions.

Constraints: must reuse existing tracing components where possible (span rows, time ruler), fit into the Console's right-hand request detail rail, support streaming trace updates, and be responsive for narrow widths (>=760px). Accessibility: color contrast and screen reader labels for each breadcrumb token.

Deliverables: low-fidelity flow map, high-fidelity Figma prototype with interactive breadcrumbs, developer handoff spec (HTML/CSS tokens, aria roles), and a short usability script for 3 customer interviews.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive breadcrumb tokens show service & operation, duration, and error badge; clicking a token zooms the timeline to that span range
Journey map aligns span tokens to the timeline and shows branching links for parallel child spans
Quick-pivot control exposes correlated-request list (by correlation ID / header) and opens selected request in a split preview without full navigation
Keyboard navigation: tab/arrow keys move between breadcrumb tokens and expanders; Enter opens the zoom; Escape collapses expanded view
Prototype tested in 3 exploratory sessions with SRE/PM/Support and at least 2 action items captured
Performance: UI maintains <120ms interactive response when rendering a 500-span trace (measured in Chrome on standard dev machine)
